title: This $470mn nuclear startup is racing a presidential deadline, not the AI boom

content_html:
Most of the money pouring into small nuclear reactors is chasing AI data centres. This round is chasing a date.

Antares has raised $470mn, co-led by Paradigm and Caffeinated Capital, with Point72 Ventures, Shine Capital and Industrious Ventures joining. The split is $370mn of equity and $100mn of debt, Bloomberg reported.

The company was founded in 2023 and has now raised more than $600mn. It wants reactors on US military installations by 2028.

The deadline doing the work

Executive Order 14299 directs the Department of War to have a reactor operating at a domestic military installation by 30 September 2028.

That is the clock. Antares has firm contracts, a named site and a fixed date, which is an unusual position for a nuclear company of any size.

The 💜 of EU tech

The latest rumblings from the EU tech scene, a story from our wise ol' founder Boris, and some questionable AI art. It's free, every week, in your inbox. Sign up now!

The company states the reasoning plainly in its announcement. Many US bases draw power from a commercial grid under strain from rising demand, extreme weather and, as it puts it, adversary targeting.

The Air Force picked Antares under its ANPI initiative for a proposed deployment at Joint Base San Antonio. Chief executive Jordan Bramble says more military projects will be announced this year.

How small is small

The scale is easy to miss and it is the most interesting number here.

Antares reactors produce no more than one megawatt. A conventional nuclear plant makes about one gigawatt. Even among microreactors, which usually top out around 20 megawatts, Antares sits at the very small end.

A factory builds these units and ships them whole. They run for years without refuelling, and the company targets six years or more of deployed operation.

That is a different product from the reactors being built for the AI boom. Valar Atomics raised $450mn to power data centres. X-energy raised $1.02bn in a Nasdaq listing. In the UK, Nuclear Turbines raised £15mn on Monday to make industrial power cheaper.

Antares is selling resilience to soldiers, not cheap electricity to hyperscalers.

The milestone, and how to read it

In June, Antares took its Mark-0 reactor critical at Idaho National Laboratory, meaning it sustained a fission reaction.

The company calls this the first privately developed non-light-water reactor to reach criticality in the United States in more than four decades. Paradigm’s Alana Palmedo went further, calling it the first private advanced reactor criticality in decades.

Bloomberg frames it more narrowly. It reports Antares as the first participant in the Energy Department’s reactor pilot programme to produce a self-sustaining fission reaction. That is a real first, and a smaller one than the company’s wording implies.

The test ran on TRISO fuel. It validated reactor physics, reactivity control and instrumentation in a full-scale core, and it produced only a small amount of energy.

“On June 4th, we won the race to criticality, and now we’ve shifted to the race to commercialisation,” Bramble said.

What has not happened yet

No microreactor is in service anywhere in the United States. Bloomberg notes the technology remains unproven at commercial scale.

Antares does not expect a system that generates electricity until next year, when the Mark-1 is due. Criticality and useful power are separate achievements, and the company has one of them.

Bramble frames the raise as matching public money rather than replacing it, describing the $470mn as investing “one-to-one with the taxpayer” to reach commercial scale.

The bottleneck nobody mentions

Fuel is the constraint that has strangled advanced nuclear for years, and Antares moved on it in May.

It signed a long-term enrichment agreement with Urenco for High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium, which Urenco called the world’s first multi-year contract for HALEU supply.

Advanced reactors need HALEU. Western supply of it has been thin, and Russia was for years the most reliable commercial source. Locking in enrichment is arguably a harder problem than locking in capital, and it attracts a fraction of the attention.

Why this one is worth watching

Britain and Europe are running the same experiment on a different footing. A Polish billionaire’s £35bn plan for 14 mini reactors targets first power in 2034, six years after Antares plans to be switched on at a US airbase.

The gap is not technical so much as procedural. American defence procurement has produced a hard deadline, a named customer and a signed contract, which is a faster mechanism than a competitive energy market.

Whether the reactor works on time is a separate question. Antares has made a fission reaction happen in a laboratory in Idaho and has not yet made a watt of useful electricity anywhere.

流入小型核反应堆的大部分资金都在追逐人工智能数据中心。 这一轮是在追约会。

Antares 已筹集 4.7 亿美元资金，由 Paradigm 和 Caffelined Capital 共同领投，Point72 Ventures、Shine Capital 和 Industrious Ventures 也跟投。 据彭博社报道，此次拆分包括 3.7 亿美元的股权和 1 亿美元的债务。

空军根据其 ANPI 计划选择 Antares 部署在圣安东尼奥联合基地。 首席执行官乔丹·布兰布尔表示，今年将宣布更多军事项目。

多小才算小

刻度很容易被忽略，它是这里最有趣的数字。

Antares 反应堆的发电量不超过一兆瓦。 一座传统核电站的发电量约为一吉瓦。 即使在通常最高功率约为 20 兆瓦的微反应堆中，Antares 也处于非常小的一端。

工厂制造这些单元并将其整体运输。 它们可以在不加油的情况下运行多年，该公司的目标是部署运行六年或更长时间。

这与为人工智能繁荣而建造的反应堆是不同的产品。 Valar Atomics 筹集了 4.5 亿美元，用于为数据中心供电。 X-energy 在纳斯达克上市筹集了 10.2 亿美元。 在英国，Nuclear Turbines 周一筹集了 1500 万英镑，以降低工业电力的成本。

Antares 正在向士兵出售弹性，而不是向超大规模企业出售廉价电力。

里程碑以及如何阅读它

6 月，Antares 爱达荷国家实验室的 Mark-0 反应堆出现临界状态，这意味着它持续进行裂变反应。

该公司称这是美国四十多年来第一个达到临界状态的私人开发的非轻水反应堆。 Paradigm 的 Alana Palmedo 更进一步，称其为数十年来首个达到临界状态的私人先进反应堆。

彭博社的框架更为狭隘。 据报道，Antares 是能源部反应堆试点计划的第一个参与者，该计划旨在产生自持裂变反应。 这是真正的第一次，而且规模比该公司的措辞所暗示的要小。

测试使用 TRISO 燃料。 它验证了全尺寸堆芯中的反应堆物理、反应性控制和仪器仪表，并且仅产生少量能量。

“6 月 4 日，我们赢得了关键性竞赛，现在我们已经转向商业化竞赛，”布兰布尔说。

还没有发生什么

美国任何地方都没有使用微反应器。 彭博社指出，该技术尚未在商业规模上得到验证。

Antares 预计要到明年 Mark-1 交付时才会有发电系统。 关键性和有用性是不同的成就，而公司拥有其中之一。

布兰堡将此次融资视为匹配公共资金，而不是取代公共资金，并将 4.7 亿美元描述为“与纳税人一对一”投资，以达到商业规模。

无人提及的瓶颈

多年来，燃料是制约先进核能发展的一个制约因素，而 Antares 在 5 月份开始解决这个问题。

它与 Urenco 签署了一份高含量低浓缩铀长期浓缩协议，Urenco 称其为世界上第一份 HALEU 供应多年期合同。

先进反应堆需要 HALEU。 西方的供应量一直很少，而俄罗斯多年来一直是最可靠的商业来源。 锁定财富可以说是比锁定资本更难的问题，而且它只吸引了一小部分注意力。

为什么这个值得一看

英国和欧洲正在不同的基础上进行同样的实验。 一位波兰亿万富翁计划耗资 350 亿英镑建造 14 座小型反应堆，目标是在 2034 年首次发电，也就是 Antares 计划在美国空军基地启动的六年后。

差距与其说是技术上的，不如说是程序上的。 美国国防采购制定了严格的最后期限、指定客户和签署的合同，这是比竞争性能源市场更快的机制。

反应堆是否按时运行是一个单独的问题。 Antares 已经在爱达荷州的一个实验室中进行了裂变反应，但尚未在任何地方产生一瓦有用的电力。
